title: How to start
summary: A club, a coach, a first lesson and a hired gun: a step-by-step plan for anyone who wants to try Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting.

body.html: Start by finding a shooting ground or a club near you. Call or write and ask whether they run sessions for beginners. Many grounds offer a taster lesson with a coach, a gun and cartridges included.

It is wise to have your first session with a coach. A coach explains the safety rules and chooses a gun that suits your size. They also show you how to stand and how to do the gun mount: bringing the stock (the rear part of the gun) to your cheek and shoulder. You start with simple, slow targets, so you see progress quickly and avoid bad habits. More: First lessons and choosing a coach.

You do not need your own gun at first. At many grounds you can hire a gun and shoot under an instructor's supervision. Gun and ammunition laws differ between countries. In some, a beginner may shoot a club gun under supervision without a licence; in others, documents are needed. Ask the ground in advance.
What to bring: comfortable clothes for the weather, closed shoes and a cap. Bring an ID document if the ground asks for one.

Wear safety glasses and hearing protection (ear muffs or earplugs) from the very first shot. Competition rules make both compulsory. If you have none, the ground can usually lend them. More: Eye and ear protection.

Do not rush to buy a gun. First try different models and ask your coach. For FITASC competitions you need a smooth-bore shotgun (no rifling inside the barrels), no larger than 12 gauge; narrower bores such as 20 or 28 are allowed. The barrels must be at least 66 cm (26 in) long, and pump-action guns (reloaded by sliding the fore-end) are not allowed. More: Choosing your first gun.
After a few lessons, try a club shoot for beginners. It is a good way to feel the atmosphere of the sport, meet people and see how referees and squads work.

key_points.html: Start at a ground with a coach and a taster lesson.
You can hire a gun; gun laws depend on the country.
Safety glasses and hearing protection from the first shot.
Buy a gun only after trying several and asking your coach.

did_you_know.html: Clay guns are often fitted to the shooter: the length and height of the stock are adjusted so the gun comes up naturally. This is called gun fit.

quiz.q: Which first step does this lesson suggest?

options.text: Buy a gun and practise alone
A taster lesson with a coach
Watch videos, then enter a championship

quiz.explain: A coach teaches safety and good basics from the very start.

quiz.q: Does a beginner need their own gun?

options.text: Yes, grounds do not lend guns
Yes, and it must be a pump-action
No, many grounds hire guns out

quiz.explain: Many grounds have club guns you can shoot under supervision; the rules depend on national law.

quiz.q: Which gun is NOT allowed in FITASC competitions?
quiz.explain: Pump-action guns are not allowed. A semi-automatic is allowed, but it may be loaded with two cartridges at most.
